criteria.criterion: Every line of the brief's worked example under `# C1` and `# C3` (but `command -$v git push`, which is T2's) gives exactly the answer and exit code the brief shows through `vloop fence check --tool bash`, in the phase it names.
criteria.evidence: TestCompoundCommands (judge_test.go) holds the C1/C3 lines as named cases with exact reasons; the go check passed.

criteria.criterion: Opening keywords (`if`, `then`, `elif`, `else`, `while`, `until`, `do`, `!`, `{`) are dropped only while they are the command's first word, before assignments are skipped; a keyword after an assignment or a wrapper is not dropped (`X=1 if true` and `env ! git status` keep `shell syntax … cannot be judged`), and one in an argument is an argument (`echo if` is an `echo`). Violation: a keyword dropped from the middle of a command.
criteria.evidence: judge.go words() drops the leading keywords before the assignment loop; cases keyword-after-assignment, keyword-after-wrapper, echo-keyword.

criteria.criterion: `fi`, `done` and `}` alone are allowed once their redirections are (`done > .vloop/state/x` is denied in a review session as a write); followed by any other word they answer `shell syntax <word> cannot be judged`. `for NAME` and `for NAME in WORDS…` (NAME matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) run nothing; any other `for` answers `shell syntax for cannot be judged`.
criteria.evidence: judge.go words() switch on fi/done/}/for with forName; cases closing-alone, done-write, brace-word, for-name, for-in, for-bare, for-bad-name, for-not-in.

criteria.criterion: `case`, `esac`, `select`, `function`, `coproc` and `[[` stay refused with `shell syntax <word> cannot be judged`, first or after an opening keyword. Violation: any of them allowed.
criteria.evidence: keywords map is unchanged; cases select, case-after-bang, dbl-bracket.

criteria.criterion: A `(` opens a subshell only when no word is being built and the current command holds nothing but opening keywords and no redirection (complete or pending); a `)` with one open ends the command and may be followed by a redirection or an operator, not a word; subshells nest written apart. `((`, a `(` anywhere else (`a=(1 2)`, `f() {`, `<(`, `>(`), a `)` with none open and a string ending with one open answer `subshells and process substitution cannot be judged`; `$(` and a backtick keep `command substitution cannot be judged`.
criteria.evidence: split.go lexer.opens(), depth and closed fields, the `((` check, and the check for an open subshell at end of string; cases nested-subshell, array, open-subshell, process-subst, subshell-word, stray-close, func-def, subst-in-subshell, arith.

criteria.criterion: A command inside a compound or a subshell is judged exactly as it would be alone: `if true; then git push; fi`, `(git push)` and `while true; do git push; done` each give `git push is denied by the review fence (Bash(git push:*))`. Violation: any inner command judged less than alone.
criteria.evidence: The splitter yields each inner command to the same words() path; cases inside-if, inside-subshell, inside-while.

criteria.criterion: When the judge looks through `command` and an option before the name is a literal `-` followed only by `p`, `v` and `V` with at least one `v` or `V` (no `$`, no quote), the command is allowed whatever follows; `command '-v' git push`, `command -p git push` and `command git push` are looked through as today; `time -v git push` stays denied.
criteria.evidence: skipCommand with the plain[] flags and lookupOption; cases command-v, command-pv, command-quoted-v, command-p, command-plain, time-v.

criteria.criterion: The hook (`vloop fence hook`) gives the same answers, since it uses the same judge; no change to the hook's own code is needed or made beyond what the judge provides.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only judge.go, split.go and judge_test.go.

criteria.criterion: Committed tests in internal/fence/judge_test.go hold every C1 and C3 worked-example line as a named case (the phase, the command, the reason) and cover the closing-keyword, for and subshell rules above; the `go` check runs them. Violation: behaviour shipped with no committed test the check runs.
criteria.evidence: The compoundCases table and TestCompoundCommands; the go check exited 0.

criteria.criterion: The existing tests pass unchanged except the cases the brief's Constraints name: in TestSplitRefuses `(gh x)` gives way to `(gh x` and `a=(1 2)`; in the work fence's table `for f in a b; do echo $f; done` becomes allowed; `if true; then gh x; fi` stays denied, its case keeping `*`.
criteria.evidence: The diff changes only the TestSplitRefuses entry and the work-table for-case; the `if true; then gh x; fi` case is untouched.

criteria.criterion: No module dependency is added to go.mod (no shell-grammar parser such as mvdan.cc/sh); no fence rule file under fence/ changes.
criteria.evidence: git status shows no go.mod or fence/ change.
